basic_info: Elizabeth, 28 years old, chief complaint: pain in the right knee following a skiing injury two weeks ago
present_illness: Onset two weeks ago during skiing, pain on the inside of the right knee, swelling, stiffness, especially in the morning, heard a pop at the time of injury. Reports intermittent instability, no locking, and no difficulty bearing weight. History of prior right knee surgery at age 14 for reconstruction following a gymnastics-related tear. Patient reports that instability occurs with specific movements or activities, which need to be clarified. Patient denies fever, fatigue, or weight loss since the injury. Patient has been managing pain with a brace and THC cream, but has not had any imaging studies done yet. Instability occurs when twisting or bending the knee, especially during walking or moving the leg sideways, and is worse in the morning and after activity. Patient denies locking or catching sensations in the knee. Swelling is consistent around the inside of the right knee, and tenderness is most prominent on the inside, near where the pop occurred when twisting the knee. The pop was pretty loud, like a snap, and it happened right when I twisted my knee into the tree. Since then, I can still bend my knee, but it's not as smooth as before. It feels stiff, especially in the morning, and sometimes I have trouble moving it the same way I did before.
past_history: Previous right knee surgery at age 14 for reconstruction following a gymnastics-related tear; no prior issues since then. No known allergies or other significant medical history.
